title: Flipkart
author: MAYANK CHANDRAKAR
body:
Flipkart Placement Experience

A stage-wise account and preparation tips for juniors

I’m sharing my experience of the Flipkart placement process to help juniors understand what to expect and how they can prepare. My process had three stages: an online assessment, a technical interview, and an HR interview. The questions can vary from person to person, especially depending on the resume and the answers given during the interview, so treat this as a guide rather than a fixed question list.

1. Online Assessment (OA)

The online assessment mainly covered technical questions related to Excel and supply chain, along with basic aptitude and English questions. There was also a supply chain case study.

How to prepare

Revise basic Excel concepts and commonly used functions.

Go through supply chain fundamentals and practise case-study-based questions.

Practise basic aptitude and English questions.

2. Technical Interview

The first interview began with my introduction. The interviewer then asked questions about my internship, particularly the results I achieved and the numbers or data I had derived from my work. There were a few follow-up questions based on my answers.

After that, the interviewer asked situation-based questions, including:

“If your senior manager disagrees with your project, how would you convince them?” I answered by explaining a similar situation that I had experienced during my previous internship.

“What would you do or change during your first 30 days as an intern in the warehouse?”

“How would you implement AI in warehouse systems to improve efficiency?”

My recommendations for this round

Prepare your answers using the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, and Result.

Be ready to explain every important project and internship on your resume, especially the outcomes, results, and numbers. You should be comfortable discussing them without having to search for details.

Prepare around 30–40 situational questions and practise answering them with real examples from your own experience.

Read about Flipkart’s core values and prepare stories from your experience that demonstrate those values.

For technical preparation, revise basic Excel, Lean Six Sigma, and supply chain theory.

3. HR Interview

The second interview was a basic HR round. After my introduction, the interviewer picked up a few points from my resume. I mentioned that I had started my own e-commerce brand and managed its end-to-end operations, so most of the discussion focused on that experience.

My experience was that the questions were closely linked to the candidate’s resume and the follow-up answers. Different candidates may therefore have different interview experiences.

Overall Interview Experience

Both interviews lasted approximately 20–25 minutes each.

In my experience, neither interview was extremely technical; the discussion focused more on my experience, the results I had achieved, and how I approached practical situations.

Your resume matters a lot, because interviewers may build much of the conversation around the projects, internships, and experiences you mention.

Final Advice for Juniors

Prepare your resume thoroughly and make sure you can explain the impact of your work with clear examples and numbers. Practise structured answers using the STAR method, revise the basics of Excel and supply chain, and prepare for situational questions. Most importantly, use genuine examples from your own experiences rather than memorising generic answers. The process may differ for each candidate, but being clear about your own work will help you handle follow-up questions with confidence.

title: Flipkart Neev AM
author: PRANAV ARORA
body:
Getting selected for the Flipkart NEEV program was a great learning experience. The selection process included an online assessment followed by an interview. The OA mainly tested aptitude, logical reasoning, and basic Excel concepts. For the interview, I focused on understanding my resume thoroughly, along with Excel, supply chain management, warehouse operations, and Lean Six Sigma concepts.

The interview included questions about my internships and projects, along with situational and behavioral questions related to teamwork, problem-solving, ownership, and handling challenges. I was also asked about my comfort with operations and warehouse-related roles.

My biggest takeaway was the importance of knowing your resume well and being clear about your fundamentals. I would recommend juniors to start preparation early, practice Excel regularly, understand their projects deeply, and prepare real examples for behavioral questions. Most importantly, stay consistent and don't get discouraged by setbacks.

title: Flipkart NEEV (Assistant Manager)
author: KANIKA RATTAN
body:
The Flipkart NEEV program targets high-potential talent for supply chain and operational roles. The selection process generally consists of an online assessment test followed by technical and behavioral interview rounds.

Round 1: Online Assessment (Aptitude & Technical)

Format: Multiple-choice assessment along with a case study testing quantitative aptitude, data interpretation, logical reasoning, and basic domain knowledge.

Tip: Time management is crucial. Practicing standard quantitative and analytical reasoning questions will help clear this round.

Round 2: Technical & Operational Interview

Format: One-on-one interview with a senior operational lead or supply chain manager.

Key Focus Areas:

In-depth walk-through of projects, internships, and technical skills listed on your resume.

Core concepts of supply chain management, logistics, and process optimization (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, inventory planning).

Case-based scenario questions assessing your analytical thinking and ability to handle operational bottlenecks.

Tip: Use data and structured frameworks (like root-cause analysis or the ECRS framework) when answering scenario-based questions.

Round 3: Managerial & HR Interview

Format: Final evaluation round focusing on leadership qualities, situational awareness, and cultural fit.

Key Questions Asked:

"Describe a situation where you managed a team under tight deadlines or high pressure."

"Why Flipkart, and what draws you to supply chain operations?"

"Why Flipkart after Textile Technology"?

Key Takeaways for Preparation

Know Your Resume: Be ready to explain every detail, metric, and responsibility mentioned in your CV.

Understand Flipkart's Ecosystem: Gain a basic understanding of e-commerce supply chain logistics (Fulfillment Centers, Last Mile, City Logistics).

Communication & Confidence: Focus on clear, logical communication and demonstrate agility to adapt to dynamic operational environments.

title: Flipkart NEEV — Managerial Role Interview Experience
author: RATISH BEHKI
body:
Company: Flipkart

Role: NEEV – Managerial/Supply Chain

Mode: Online

Process: OA + 2 Interviews

OA Round

- MS Excel questions

- 1 Supply Chain-based question

- General MCQs from Physics, Maths, Aptitude, etc.

- Conducted completely online.

Interview 1 — HR + Technical (~30 min)

Mostly resume + supply chain based.

Asked about:

- Internships: role, challenges faced, efficiency improvements

- How Flipkart's supply chain works

- A situation with phones priced at ₹25k, ₹50k and ₹1 lakh — which would sell more and why?

- My answer: ₹25k likely has higher volume due to affordability; ₹1 lakh may see higher demand during occasions/offers. Customers consider model, colour, features, discounts, etc.

- If managing 30 hubs in Bengaluru, what common requirements would they have?

- Manpower, warehouses, transportation, inventory/order handling, etc.

- Ended with: “Do you have any questions for us?”

Interview 2 — HR + Operations (~15–20 min)

Asked:

- About Flipkart

- Tell me about yourself

- Why switch from Mechanical to a Managerial/Supply Chain role?

- Supply chain concepts: Kaizen, Pareto Analysis, Six Sigma

- Situation-based questions:

- How would you handle last-minute deliveries at Kartarpur hub?

- What would you do if fraud occurs in the process?

- If you become a manager in the morning and have to clear all pending orders by 9 PM, what actions would you take?

- Explain the supply chain from the hub → delivery executive → customer and the people involved.

Key Preparation

Focus on:

Supply Chain + Logistics + Warehousing + Last-mile delivery + Excel + Kaizen + Pareto + Six Sigma + HR/Situational questions.

Most importantly, know your resume well and be ready to explain your internships/projects, challenges and how you improved efficiency.

title: Flipkart NEEV
author: KUNWAR ABHAY MEHRA
body: I got placed at Flipkart as an Assistant Manager – NEEV through the campus placement process. The process included an assessment round, interview rounds, and an HR discussion. The role is focused on supply chain and operations, providing an opportunity to work on areas such as process management, operational efficiency, data-driven decision-making, and coordination across different functions. Overall, the placement process helped me explore supply chain as a career domain and ultimately led to an opportunity with Flipkart.

title: Flipkart Assistant Manager (NEEV) Role
author: NISHITA NITIN GAIKWAD
body:
Round 1 – Online Assessment (OA)

The first round was an Online Assessment conducted on the HirePro platform. There were two slots available: 6:00 PM and 9:00 PM. The OA included aptitude, technical, and guesstimate-based questions. Guesstimate question required us to calculate and enter the answer rather than simply choosing an option.

Round 2 – Interview 1: Resume & Role-Based

This round focused mainly on resume, communication, confidence, and basic supply-chain knowledge. Questions included:

Tell me about yourself and your projects.

What do you mean by e-commerce?

Basic terminologies of Supply Chain mgmt were asked.

Why Flipkart?

Why the Assistant Manager – NEEV role?

What do you understand about the Assistant Manager role?

What would your responsibilities be if selected?

Where do you see yourself in five years?

Basic questions related to my resume and projects.

Round 3 – Technical & Case-Based Interview

This was the technical/functional round and included case-based and situational questions. I was asked about the 4M method (Man, Machine, Method, Material) and its application to real-world operational problems, such as delays in packaging and task completion. Questions also covered employee management, conflict resolution, and problem-solving. My internship was discussed in detail, along with questions on data analysis and its applications in the domain, projects, hobbies, and extracurricular activities.

Round 4 – HR / Fitment Round

The final round was a telephonic HR/fitment round. It included basic resume-based questions, family/background questions, experience or exposure related to the e-commerce sector, and questions checking my understanding of the job description and role. It was mainly a final fitment discussion.

Final Result

There were a few days of gap between the interview rounds. The final result was communicated approximately 3–4 days after the last round.
